title: Descent of uniquely normalized diagonal-class isomorphisms on an open basis
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $Y=X\times_SX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with first projection $p_1$ and closed diagonal $\Delta$, and put $D=\Delta_*\mathcal O_X[0]$. Let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and let $\xi:D\to Lp_1^*K$ and $\eta:D\to Lp_1^*L$ be morphisms [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Suppose multiplication by $\eta$ is an isomorphism $D\to R\mathcal Hom_Y(D,Lp_1^*L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; multiplication means the transpose of the derived multiplication $D\otimes^{\mathbf L}D\to D$ followed by $\eta$, as in [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a set of opens forming a basis for $X$, meaning every open of $X$ is a union of members of $\mathcal B$. For each $U\in\mathcal B$ assume $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K|_U,K|_U[i])=0$ for every $i<0$ and assume there is exactly one isomorphism $\alpha_U:K|_U\to L|_U$ for which $(Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha_U)\xi_U=\eta_U$ on $U\times_SU$. Here $p_{1,U}$ and $\Delta_U$ are the projection and diagonal for $U/S$, and $\xi_U,\eta_U$ are the restrictions under the canonical identifications of diagonal direct image and derived pullback with open restriction. Then the $\alpha_U$ are compatible with inclusions of basis opens, and there is exactly one isomorphism $\alpha:K\to L$ restricting to all the $\alpha_U$. There is a canonical $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$-linear identification $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(D,Lp_1^*L)\cong\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ sending $\eta$ to $1$, compatible with restriction to every basis open. The resulting global isomorphism satisfies $(Lp_1^*\alpha)\xi=\eta$, and it is the unique isomorphism with this equality. No quasi-compactness, finite-cover or affine-intersection hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: If $V\subset U$ are basis opens, restrict $(Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha_U)\xi_U=\eta_U$ to $V\times_S V$. The canonical restriction identifications in the hypotheses give $(Lp_{1,V}^*(\alpha_U|_V))\xi_V=\eta_V$. Restriction preserves an inverse, so $\alpha_U|_V$ is an isomorphism. The assumed uniqueness on $V$ gives $\alpha_U|_V=\alpha_V$. In particular the inverse family is inclusion-compatible too. The basis covers $X$, and its members contained in $U\cap V$ cover $U\cap V$, by the definition of a basis.

source.place: Tag 0E2W (lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing), final gluing paragraph: compatibility of the unique normalized local maps

proof.text: On a basis open $U$, the given $\alpha_U$ identifies $L|_U$ with $K|_U$. Composing with this isomorphism and its shifts identifies every negative cross Hom for $(K,L)$ or $(L,K)$, and every negative self Hom for $L$, with the assumed zero group for $K$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] with $O=X$ to the compatible families $\alpha_U$ and $\alpha_U^{-1}$ to obtain $a:K\to L$ and $b:L\to K$. Apply its injectivity clause to $(K,K)$ and $(L,L)$: the restrictions of $ba$ and $ab$ are the respective identities, hence $ba=1_K$ and $ab=1_L$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism. The same Hom bijection for $(K,L)$ says that it is the unique morphism restricting to all $\alpha_U$.

Write $A=\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$, $D=A[0]$, $M=Lp_1^*L$, $\mu=\mu_Y(A,A);Qt:D\otimes^{\mathbf L}D\to D$ for the derived multiplication and $e=e_{-,D,M}$ for the canonical tensor--Hom bijection of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection], so that $m_\eta=e^{-1}(\mu;\eta)$ is the assumed isomorphism, as in [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. For $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=\Gamma(Y,A)$ let $\sigma_s:\mathcal O_Y\to A$ be the module map $a\mapsto as$ and $m_s:A\to A$ multiplication by $s$. A module map $\phi:\mathcal O_Y\to A$ equals $\sigma_{\phi(1)}$, since $\phi(a)=a\phi(1)$ on every open; so $s\mapsto\sigma_s$ is a bijection onto $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(\mathcal O_Y,A)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] for $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$, $s\mapsto Q\sigma_s$ is a bijection $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(\mathcal O_Y[0],D)$. Composing with the isomorphism $m_\eta$, then $e_{\mathcal O_Y[0],D,M}$ and the left unitor $\lambda_D$ of [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], gives a bijection $\Psi:\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(D,M)$, $\Psi(s)=\lambda_D^{-1};e(Q\sigma_s;m_\eta)$. Naturality of $e$ in the first variable gives $e(Q\sigma_s;m_\eta)=(Q\sigma_s\otimes1);\mu;\eta$. Naturality of $\mu_Y$ and the fact that the unitor descends from the module unitor give $\lambda_D^{-1};(Q\sigma_s\otimes1);\mu_Y(A,A);Qt=Q(d\mapsto1\otimes d\mapsto s\otimes d\mapsto sd)=Qm_s$. Hence $\Psi(s)=\eta\circ m_s$. Put $\Phi=\Psi^{-1}$. Then $\Phi(\eta)=1$, since $m_1$ is the identity. Give the Hom group its $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ action by precomposition with $m_s$. The equations $m_{s+t}=m_s+m_t$ and $m_sm_t=m_{st}$ show that $\Phi$ is linear.

proof.text: For $U\in\mathcal B$ put $Y_U=U\times_S U$. On an open $W\subset Y_U$, the equality $(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X)(W)=\mathcal O_X(\Delta^{-1}W)=\mathcal O_U(\Delta_U^{-1}W)$ identifies $D|_{Y_U}$ with $D_U=\Delta_{U,*}\mathcal O_U[0]$, preserving products and the unit. Use the pullback restriction identification stipulated in the statement for $M|_{Y_U}$. The internal-Hom comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and the transposition equation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] identify $m_\eta|_{Y_U}$ with multiplication by $\eta_U$: both transpose the restricted multiplication followed by the restricted class. Writing $\theta:rR\mathcal Hom_Y(D,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{Y_U}(rD,rM)$ for that comparison, the cited equation gives $m_{\eta_U}=\theta\circ r(m_\eta)$ after the stipulated identifications. Both factors are isomorphisms, hence so is $m_{\eta_U}$. Apply the construction of Step 3 on the scheme $Y_U$, using [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] and [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], to get $\Phi_U$. Its inverse formula is $s_U\mapsto\eta_U\circ m_{s_U}$. Restricting $\Phi^{-1}(s)=\eta\circ m_s$ gives exactly $\eta_U\circ m_{s|_U}$. Consequently $\Phi_U(h|_{Y_U})=\Phi(h)|_U$ for every global class $h$.

Let $h=(Lp_1^*a)\xi$ and $s=\Phi(h)$. Since $a|_U=\alpha_U$, the stipulated pullback identifications and local normalization give $h|_{Y_U}=\eta_U$. Step 4 therefore gives $s|_U=\Phi_U(\eta_U)=1$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$. These opens cover $X$, so the separatedness axiom of the structure sheaf gives $s=1$. Step 3 now gives $h=\Phi^{-1}(1)=\eta$. This argument uses a cover of $X$; it requires no assertion that the opens $Y_U$ cover $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0E2W (lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing), final sentence, with scalar detection made explicit

proof.text: If $c:K\to L$ is any isomorphism satisfying $(Lp_1^*c)\xi=\eta$, restrict this equation to $Y_U$. Then $c|_U$ is a normalized isomorphism, so the uniqueness hypothesis gives $c|_U=\alpha_U$. The uniqueness already proved in Step 2 gives $c=a$. All the constructions include the empty scheme and an empty basis there: its module category has one object and morphism, and its section ring is the zero ring, where $1=0$. No step uses a finite subcover, quasi-compactness or affine intersections.
